base_member_text: Cross-line: FORMAT_LEN is built once under the SAVEd FirstCallPutFile flag (L85-92) but FORMAT_LEN itself is the CHARACTER(LEN=16) from MODULE GLOBAL (USE GLOBAL L56); the format count field uses Mglob but the write loop strides by OUTPUT_RES (L146), so for OUTPUT_RES>1 the format repeat count exceeds the items written - harmless in Fortran but the format does not reflect the decimated width.
PHIGLOB(MGlob,NGlob) is an automatic (stack) array on every rank (L79), not just rank 0 - large-grid stack usage on all ranks; the commented alternative with ghost dimensions is at L78.
PutFileASCII derived-type/inner loop assumes iista:iiend gathered ranges tile MGlob x NGlob exactly (L114, L128); no overlap/coverage check is performed.
PutFileBinary declares PHITEST (L166) and istatus (L168) but never uses them; ierr from MPI calls is never checked in either subroutine.
PutFileBinary writes raw 'native' mpi_sp records with no header; the byte layout/global-size metadata must be known by the post-processor - external convention.
The nonblocking mpi_irecv/mpi_isend pairs are each immediately mpi_wait'ed (L125-126, L134-135), making them effectively blocking; ireq is reused across iterations.
END SUBROUTINE names use different capitalization (PutfileASCII L157, PutfileBinary L221) than the declarations (L60, L161) - legal in Fortran, purely cosmetic.

audit_member_text: PutFileBinary opens with MPI_MODE_WRONLY + MPI_MODE_CREATE (L208-L210) and writes the current global view (L213-L218) but never calls MPI_FILE_SET_SIZE or otherwise truncates an already-existing file; if a later output is smaller, stale trailing bytes can remain.

PutFileASCII uses OUTPUT_RES as both outer and implied-DO stride (L144-L145) without any local positivity/range check; OUTPUT_RES=0 is an invalid DO step and a negative value suppresses the expected traversal.
